payload.hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise binary cross-entropy objective with a within-user listwise softmax (cross-entropy over each user's impression group, normalised by the group's positive count) raises validation primary by at least +0.004 over the 0.60147 baseline, with the same five fields and k=16.
payload.mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 depend only on the ordering of scores inside a user's group. A softmax over a user's group has gradients that depend only on score differences within that group, so every unit of gradient goes into the quantity the metric measures; any per-user additive offset is cancelled. Pointwise logloss instead pushes each row toward the global base rate, and a large part of that gradient moves a user-constant term that C2 proves cannot change the score. Concentrating the loss on within-user contrasts should therefore sharpen the ordering of mixed-label users, which carry 100% of GAUC weight and most of the movable nDCG mass.
payload.predicted: +0.004 to +0.010 valid primary (0.605-0.611); anything below +0.002 counts as a null result for this formulation.
payload.invalid_if: Validation primary with pure listwise (alpha=0) lands within +/-0.002 of 0.60147 across 3 matched seeds AND the 0.5-mixed variant does the same — i.e. the objective is not the bottleneck it is claimed to be.
evidence: Organizer's own judged headroom list ranks loss/objective mismatch first: training is pointwise logloss while the metric is a within-user ranking metric (RULES §5, README).
C2/C23: only within-user ordering matters; a pointwise probability objective spends capacity on cross-user calibration that is provably a no-op for the metric.
C9: 57.778% of validation users are mixed-label and hold 78.907% of rows, so most users supply a well-formed listwise group with at least one positive and one negative.
C6/C5: capacity and static-feature expansion are both dead ends in this FM, so the remaining lever in the same model class is the objective.
C8: the baseline reproduces at 0.60147 with seed std 0.00032 locally / 0.0008 published, so a +0.004 delta is clearly outside noise.
payload.reason: Pure within-user softmax scored 0.59874 vs parent 0.60147, a paired delta of -0.00273: about 5 sigma below the noise floor and past the 0.002 practical threshold, so the sign is real and opposite to the predicted +0.004..+0.010. The invalid_if clause is not met (this is not a null, it is a regression), so the claim 'the objective is the bottleneck' is refuted for this exact formulation. The decomposition is informative: GAUC fell 0.0045 (0.66713 -> 0.66291) while nDCG@5 fell only 0.0010 (0.53581 -> 0.53456). GAUC is scored exclusively on mixed-label users, i.e. precisely the population this loss trains on, so the loss did not merely fail to help the users it targeted, it hurt them. That points at the implementation of the objective rather than at the metric-alignment argument. Two concrete confounds are visible in the diff and were not controlled: (1) every uniform-label group is skipped, so with alpha=0 roughly 42% of users and ~21% of rows contribute zero gradient and all first-order/popularity signal carried by those rows is discarded; (2) the gradient is renormalised per batch by n_groups rather than by row count, and softmax residuals (p - t) live on a different scale than sigmoid residuals, so lr=0.001, 40 epochs and patience=4 — all tuned for pointwise BCE — no longer describe the same optimisation problem. A regression under an untuned step size and a 21% smaller effective training set does not isolate the objective.
payload.mechanism_update: C2 (within-user invariance) remains true and still implies pointwise BCE spends gradient on user-constant terms, but this run shows that gradient is not simply wasted. Under a five-field FM the user-constant mass is carried by shared embeddings (video_id, author_id, tab, dur_bucket appear across users), so a pointwise fit to the global base rate is also fitting item-side popularity that transfers between users; a strictly within-user contrast throws that cross-user calibration away and, at this data scale and sparsity (98.4% of validation user-item pairs are novel), the item-side prior is doing real work. The practical lesson is that 'the metric only sees within-user order' does not license 'training signal should only be within-user order' — the two are separated by generalisation across users. Additionally, swapping a loss silently changes the gradient scale, so any loss experiment on this repo must re-tune lr/epochs or it is confounded.
deprioritise: pure listwise softmax with alpha=0 at the inherited lr=0.001 / 40-epoch / patience-4 schedule
per-group (n_groups) gradient normalisation that equalises users regardless of list length — it upweights the median-4-impression tail against the long lists holding most GAUC weight
any further loss variant run at the baseline schedule without a matched lr sweep

+"""模型架构 —— 唯一允许改模型/损失函数的地方。见 AGENT_RULES.md。
+
+对外契约（train.py 依赖这些）：
+    FM(dim, k=16, lr=0.001, l2=1e-6, seed=0)
+        .step(X, y) -> loss:float      # 一个 mini-batch 的梯度更新（pointwise BCE）
+        .step_listwise(X, y, offsets, alpha=0.0) -> loss:float
+                                       # 组内 softmax 列表损失（可混 pointwise）
+        .predict(X, bs=200_000) -> np.ndarray[float]   # 打分，越大越相关
+        .V, .W, .b                     # 供 train.py 做 best-checkpoint 保存/恢复
+"""
+import numpy as np
+
+def sigmoid(x):
+    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(x, -30, 30)))
+
+class FM:
+    def __init__(self, dim, k=16, lr=0.001, l2=1e-6, seed=0):
+        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+        self.V = rng.normal(0, 0.01, (dim, k)).astype(np.float32)
+        self.W = np.zeros(dim, dtype=np.float32)
+        self.b = np.float32(0.0)
+        self.lr, self.l2 = lr, l2
+        self.mV = np.zeros_like(self.V); self.vV = np.zeros_like(self.V)
+        self.mW = np.zeros_like(self.W); self.vW = np.zeros_like(self.W)
+        self.t = 0
+
+    def logits(self, X):
+        E = self.V[X]                                   # (B,F,k)
+        S = E.sum(1)                                    # (B,k)
+        inter = 0.5 * ((S ** 2).sum(1) - (E ** 2).sum((1, 2)))
+        return self.b + self.W[X].sum(1) + inter, E, S
+
+    # ---- 共用的参数更新：给定 dL/dz（每行一个标量），写回 W/V/b ----
+    def _apply(self, g, X, E, S):
+        g = g.astype(np.float32)
+        gV = np.zeros_like(self.V); gW = np.zeros_like(self.W)
+        np.add.at(gW, X, g[:, None])
+        np.add.at(gV, X, g[:, None, None] * (S[:, None, :] - E))
+        gV += self.l2 * self.V; gW += self.l2 * self.W
+        self.t += 1
+        b1, b2, eps = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
+        for P, G, M, Vv in ((self.V, gV, self.mV, self.vV), (self.W, gW, self.mW, self.vW)):
+            M *= b1; M += (1 - b1) * G
+            Vv *= b2; Vv += (1 - b2) * (G * G)
+            P -= self.lr * (M / (1 - b1 ** self.t)) / (np.sqrt(Vv / (1 - b2 ** self.t)) + eps)
+        self.b -= self.lr * float(g.sum())
+
+    def step(self, X, y):
+        B = len(y)
+        z, E, S = self.logits(X)
+        g = ((sigmoid(z) - y) / B).astype(np.float32)    # (B,)
+        self._apply(g, X, E, S)
+        return float(-np.mean(y * np.log(sigmoid(z) + 1e-9) + (1 - y) * np.log(1 - sigmoid(z) + 1e-9)))
+
+    def step_listwise(self, X, y, offsets, alpha=0.0):
+        """组内 listwise softmax 交叉熵。
+
+        offsets: 长度 G+1 的递增数组，[offsets[i], offsets[i+1]) 是第 i 个用户组的行。
+        每组目标分布 t_i = y_i / n_pos（正例均分），loss = -sum_i t_i log p_i，
+        dL/dz_i = p_i - t_i —— 只依赖组内分数差，组内常数偏移自动抵消。
+        全正/全负组没有组内对比，列表项跳过（仍可通过 alpha 的 pointwise 项参与）。
+        总损失 = (1-alpha) * listwise + alpha * pointwise BCE。
+        """
+        z, E, S = self.logits(X)
+        B = len(y)
+        g = np.zeros(B, dtype=np.float32)
+        loss_list = 0.0
+        n_groups = 0
+        for a, bnd in zip(offsets[:-1], offsets[1:]):
+            a = int(a); bnd = int(bnd)
+            n = bnd - a
+            if n < 2:
+                continue
+            yy = y[a:bnd]
+            npos = float(yy.sum())
+            if npos <= 0.0 or npos >= n:
+                continue
+            zz = z[a:bnd]
+            zz = zz - zz.max()
+            e = np.exp(zz)
+            p = e / e.sum()
+            t = yy / npos
+            g[a:bnd] += (p - t).astype(np.float32)
+            loss_list += -float(np.sum(t * np.log(p + 1e-9)))
+            n_groups += 1
+        if n_groups > 0:
+            scale = (1.0 - alpha) / n_groups
+            g *= np.float32(scale)
+            loss_list /= n_groups
+        else:
+            g[:] = 0.0
+            loss_list = 0.0
+
+        loss_point = 0.0
+        if alpha > 0.0:
+            s = sigmoid(z)
+            g += (alpha * (s - y) / B).astype(np.float32)
+            loss_point = float(-np.mean(y * np.log(s + 1e-9) + (1 - y) * np.log(1 - s + 1e-9)))
+
+        self._apply(g, X, E, S)
+        return float((1.0 - alpha) * loss_list + alpha * loss_point)
+
+    def predict(self, X, bs=200_000):
+        return np.concatenate([self.logits(X[i:i + bs])[0] for i in range(0, len(X), bs)])

+        out[name] = evaluate([x[IDX['user_id']] for x in rws], [x[IDX['label']] for x in rws],
+                             [score(x[IDX['video_id']]) for x in rws])
+    return out
+
+def run_random(splits, seed=0, report_test=False):
+    """report_test=False（默认）：只算 valid，理由同 run_pop。"""
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    out = {}
+    for name in (('valid', 'test') if report_test else ('valid',)):
+        rws = splits[name]
+        out[name] = evaluate([x[IDX['user_id']] for x in rws], [x[IDX['label']] for x in rws],
+                             rng.random(len(rws)))
+    return out
+
+# ---------------- listwise 分组 batching ----------------
+def _user_groups(users, y, alpha):
+    """把训练行按 user_id 分组（保持原顺序）。alpha==0（纯 listwise）时丢掉
+    全正/全负/单行组 —— 它们没有组内对比，对损失和指标都不贡献任何东西。"""
+    d = collections.OrderedDict()
+    for i, u in enumerate(users):
+        d.setdefault(u, []).append(i)
+    groups = []
+    for rows in d.values():
+        idx = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.int64)
+        if alpha <= 0.0:
+            n = len(idx)
+            npos = float(y[idx].sum())
+            if n < 2 or npos <= 0.0 or npos >= n:
+                continue
+        groups.append(idx)
+    return groups
+
+def _listwise_batches(groups, order, bs):
+    """把整组打包成 ~bs 行的 batch，给出（行索引, 组边界 offsets）。"""
+    buf, offs, n = [], [0], 0
+    for gi in order:
+        g = groups[gi]
+        buf.append(g); n += len(g); offs.append(n)
+        if n >= bs:
+            yield np.concatenate(buf), np.asarray(offs, dtype=np.int64)
+            buf, offs, n = [], [0], 0
+    if buf:
+        yield np.concatenate(buf), np.asarray(offs, dtype=np.int64)
+
+# ---------------- Factorization Machine ----------------
+def run_fm(splits, k=16, lr=0.001, epochs=40, bs=8192, patience=4, seed=0, verbose=True,
+           report_test=False, alpha=0.0):
+    """report_test=False（默认）：训练/早停/模型选择只用 valid，函数结束时也不碰 test —
+    这是 AGENT_RULES.md 规则 3 的代码落实，不是靠自觉。只有汇报最终数字时才传 True。
+    alpha: pointwise BCE 在总损失里的权重，0.0 = 纯组内 listwise softmax。"""
+    enc, dim = encode(splits)
+    Xtr, ytr, utr = enc['train']; Xva, yva, uva = enc['valid']
+    m = FM(dim, k=k, lr=lr, seed=seed)
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    groups = _user_groups(utr, ytr, alpha)
+    if verbose:
+        print(f"  listwise groups: {len(groups)} (alpha={alpha})")
+    best, best_state, bad = -1, None, 0
+    for ep in range(1, epochs + 1):
+        order = rng.permutation(len(groups)); t0 = time.time()
+        losses = [m.step_listwise(Xtr[rows], ytr[rows], offs, alpha=alpha)
+                  for rows, offs in _listwise_batches(groups, order, bs)]
+        va = evaluate(uva, yva, m.predict(Xva))
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"  epoch {ep:2d} | loss {np.mean(losses):.4f} | valid GAUC {va['GAUC']:.4f} "
+                  f"nDCG@5 {va['nDCG@5']:.4f} primary {va['primary']:.4f} | {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")
+        if va['primary'] > best + 1e-5:
+            best, bad = va['primary'], 0
+            best_state = (m.V.copy(), m.W.copy(), np.float32(m.b))
+        else:
+            bad += 1
+            if bad >= patience:
+                if verbose: print(f"  early stop at epoch {ep}")
+                break
+    m.V, m.W, m.b = best_state
+    out = {'valid': evaluate(uva, yva, m.predict(Xva))}
+    if report_test:
+        Xte, yte, ute = enc['test']
+        out['test'] = evaluate(ute, yte, m.predict(Xte))
+    return out
+
+# ---------------- harness contract ----------------
+def fit_predict(enc, dim, model='fm', k=16, lr=0.001, epochs=40, bs=8192, patience=4,
+                seed=0, verbose=False, alpha=0.0):
+    """Train on `train` and return raw scores for every split.
+
+    THE HARNESS CALLS THIS. `run_fm` above returns metrics only, which is enough for a
+    human reading stdout but not enough to build a submission — and a submission built
+    any other way (e.g. kit/submit.py --make) silently ships the untouched baseline
+    instead of whatever this pipeline learned.
+
+    Contract, preserve it when you change the model or the loss:
+        fit_predict(enc, dim, ...) -> {'train': ndarray, 'valid': ndarray, 'test': ndarray}
+    One float per row, higher = more relevant, aligned to enc[split] row order. Selection
+    and early stopping use `valid` only; `test` scores are produced but never read here.
+    """
+    Xtr, ytr, utr = enc['train']
+    Xva, yva, uva = enc['valid']
+
+    if model == 'pop':
+        pos, imp = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
+        for xrow, yrow in zip(Xtr[:, 1], ytr):          # column 1 == video_id slot
+            imp[int(xrow)] += 1; pos[int(xrow)] += yrow
+        gmean = sum(pos.values()) / max(sum(imp.values()), 1)
+        prior = 20.0
+        def sc(v):
+            v = int(v)
+            return (pos[v] + prior * gmean) / (imp[v] + prior) if imp[v] else gmean
+        return {sp: np.array([sc(v) for v in enc[sp][0][:, 1]], dtype=float) for sp in enc}
+
+    if model == 'random':
+        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+        return {sp: rng.random(len(enc[sp][1])) for sp in enc}
+
+    m = FM(dim, k=k, lr=lr, seed=seed)
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    groups = _user_groups(utr, ytr, alpha)
+    best, best_state, bad = -1, None, 0
+    for ep in range(1, epochs + 1):
+        order = rng.permutation(len(groups))
+        for rows, offs in _listwise_batches(groups, order, bs):
+            m.step_listwise(Xtr[rows], ytr[rows], offs, alpha=alpha)
+        p = evaluate(uva, yva, m.predict(Xva))['primary']
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"  epoch {ep:2d} valid primary {p:.5f}", flush=True)
+        if p > best + 1e-5:
+            best, bad = p, 0
+            best_state = (m.V.copy(), m.W.copy(), np.float32(m.b))
+        else:
+            bad += 1
+            if bad >= patience:
+                break
+    m.V, m.W, m.b = best_state
+    return {sp: m.predict(enc[sp][0]) for sp in enc}
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument('--data_dir', default='./KuaiRand-Pure/data',
+                    help='KuaiRand-Pure 解压后的 data 目录')
+    ap.add_argument('--model', default='fm', choices=['pop', 'fm', 'random'])
+    ap.add_argument('--k', type=int, default=16)
+    ap.add_argument('--lr', type=float, default=0.001)
+    ap.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=40)
+    ap.add_argument('--alpha', type=float, default=0.0,
+                    help='pointwise BCE 权重（0.0 = 纯组内 listwise softmax）')
+    ap.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0)
+    ap.add_argument('--final', action='store_true',
+                    help='也算并打印 test（只在最终汇报一次时用；开发迭代时不要加这个 flag）')

+                                   report_test=a.final, alpha=a.alpha)}[a.model](splits)

+        print(f"  {sp:5s}  GAUC {r['GAUC']:.4f} | nDCG@5 {r['nDCG@5']:.4f} | primary {r['primary']:.4f}")
payload.note: Added FM.step_listwise: per-user softmax cross-entropy with targets y/n_pos, gradient (p - t) fed through the existing FM/Adam path, with an alpha knob mixing in the old pointwise BCE (alpha=0 = pure listwise); step() is untouched. train.py now batches whole user groups (~8192 rows per batch, group order reshuffled each epoch, contrast-free groups dropped when alpha=0) in both run_fm and fit_predict, with early stopping and model selection still on validation primary.

payload.hypothesis: Adding strictly-prior behavioural aggregates (item historical long_view rate + support count, user historical long_view rate, user×tab historical rate) as bucketed FM fields raises validation primary by at least +0.002 over the 5-field baseline.
payload.mechanism: Two distinct effects, both within-user varying. (a) The video prior-rate bucket is a low-cardinality, high-count backoff for item quality: rare videos whose own embedding is under-trained inherit a well-estimated quality level, changing their position inside a user's list directly through the first-order term. (b) The user-rate and user×tab buckets pool sparse users into behavioural segments, so cross terms like user_rate_bucket x dur_bucket / x video_id let a low-activity user borrow the item preferences of similar-propensity users rather than relying on a barely-trained user embedding. Neither signal exists anywhere in the current model.
payload.predicted: +0.003 valid primary (0.6045), with GAUC moving more than nDCG@5; anything below +0.002 is a null.
payload.invalid_if: Mean validation primary over 2-3 matched seeds is <= 0.6035, or the gain is confined to the count bucket alone (i.e. the rate buckets are indistinguishable from an unknown-count indicator).
evidence: The current model uses zero behavioural history: kit.data.load() exposes only date/user/video/author/tab/duration/label (repo representation block).
harness.history.prior_stats provides leakage-safe strictly-earlier aggregates with tie exclusion, keyed on row fields or tuples (§0b).
C13: 98.114% of validation users have >=1 prior train interaction, 92.85% have >=5; videos are 99.882% warm (C12), so a video-level prior rate has near-complete support.
Item popularity alone scores 0.5807 validation primary, i.e. item-level historical signal is genuinely predictive on its own (baseline ladder).
C2 says user-constant terms are ranking no-ops, but a user-rate bucket enters the FM through pairwise cross terms with video_id/author_id/tab/dur_bucket, which do vary within a list.
C10: T1 (1-17 prior interactions) has the lowest baseline GAUC (0.6515) and holds 14.67% of GAUC weight - exactly the population an ID embedding fits worst and a pooled bucket helps most.
payload.reason: Predicted >= +0.002; measured -0.00137 on validation, about 2.7x the 0.0005 paired noise floor, so the sign is real even though the magnitude sits under the 0.002 practical epsilon. Both metrics moved down together (GAUC 0.66618 vs 0.6674, nDCG@5 0.53402 vs 0.5357), which is the signature of a globally slightly worse model rather than a redistribution between the two user populations. The invalid_if condition (mean <= 0.6035) is met. The claimed mechanism is not supported: neither the item quality-backoff bucket nor the user/user-tab pooling buckets bought anything, and they cost something.
payload.mechanism_update: Adding four coarse bucketed prior-rate/count fields to the official FM behaves like the earlier static-feature expansions (C5): more low-cardinality fields dilute the pairwise interaction budget without adding within-user-varying signal that video_id/author_id embeddings don't already carry. Two structural reasons stand out. (1) v_rate_b is a strictly coarser function of video_id, and validation videos are 99.88% warm (C12) — the population that would benefit from a high-count backoff is nearly empty, so the backoff term mostly re-encodes information the item embedding already has, while adding first-order and cross parameters that must be re-fit. (2) u_rate_b is constant within a user, so by C2 its first-order term is exactly a no-op; it can only act through crosses, and every field added to an FM multiplies the number of pairwise terms competing for the same gradient, which is a plausible route to the small regression. This does not refute prior-history features as a class — it refutes the specific 'quantile-bucket the aggregate into an extra FM categorical field' encoding, which is precisely the encoding this dataset has already rejected twice under a different name.
deprioritise: adding further coarse bucketed aggregates as extra FM categorical fields (item/user/user-tab prior rates, support counts) — same encoding, already twice negative
user-level prior aggregates encoded as first-order fields, which C2 makes structurally inert within a user
item-quality backoff motivated by cold items, given 99.88% item warmth in validation

+        edges = np.unique(np.quantile(seen, qs))
+    out = {}
+    for sp in count:
+        c = np.asarray(count[sp], dtype=float)
+        b = np.searchsorted(edges, np.log1p(c))
+        col = [f"{prefix}{int(v)}" if c[i] > 0 else f"{prefix}nh"
+               for i, v in enumerate(b)]
+        out[sp] = col
+    return out
+
+
+def _history_columns(splits):
+    """4 列严格前驱聚合，按位置与 splits[sp] 对齐。"""
+    v_rate, v_cnt = prior_stats(splits, signal='label', key='video_id')
+    u_rate, u_cnt = prior_stats(splits, signal='label', key='user_id')
+    ut_rate, ut_cnt = prior_stats(splits, signal='label', key=('user_id', 'tab'))
+
+    cols = [
+        _rate_columns(v_rate, v_cnt, 8, 'vr'),
+        _count_columns(v_cnt, 5, 'vc'),
+        _rate_columns(u_rate, u_cnt, 6, 'ur'),
+        _rate_columns(ut_rate, ut_cnt, 6, 'tr'),
+    ]
+    out = {}
+    for sp in splits:
+        out[sp] = [c[sp] for c in cols]
+    return out
+
+
+def encode(splits):
+    """把类别特征映射成连续 id。未见过的取值统一落到该域的 UNK 槽。
+    分桶边界只能用 splits['train'] 算。"""
+    tr = splits['train']
+    edges = _bucket_edges([same_row(x, 'duration_ms') for x in tr])
+    hist = _history_columns(splits)
+
+    def raw(x, extras):
+        return [same_row(x, 'user_id'), same_row(x, 'video_id'), same_row(x, 'author_id'),
+                same_row(x, 'tab'),
+                str(int(np.searchsorted(edges, same_row(x, 'duration_ms'))))] + extras
+
+    tr_hist = hist['train']
+    vocabs = [dict() for _ in FIELDS]
+    for n, x in enumerate(tr):
+        extras = [c[n] for c in tr_hist]
+        for i, v in enumerate(raw(x, extras)):
+            if v not in vocabs[i]:
+                vocabs[i][v] = len(vocabs[i])
+    unk = [len(v) for v in vocabs]                 # 每个域末尾留一个 UNK 槽
+    field_dims = [len(v) + 1 for v in vocabs]
+    offsets = np.cumsum([0] + field_dims[:-1]).astype(np.int32)
+
+    enc = {}
+    for name, rws in splits.items():
+        sp_hist = hist[name]
+        X = np.empty((len(rws), len(FIELDS)), dtype=np.int32)
+        y = np.empty(len(rws), dtype=np.float32)
+        users = []
+        for n, x in enumerate(rws):
+            extras = [c[n] for c in sp_hist]
+            for i, v in enumerate(raw(x, extras)):
+                X[n, i] = vocabs[i].get(v, unk[i]) + offsets[i]
+            y[n] = x[IDX['label']]
+            users.append(x[IDX['user_id']])
+        enc[name] = (X, y, users)
+    return enc, int(sum(field_dims))
payload.note: Added four strictly-prior history fields (video long_view rate bucket, video log-support-count bucket, user rate bucket, user×tab rate bucket) built via harness.history.prior_stats/bucketize, with all quantile edges computed from train rows only and a dedicated 'no history' level per field. Only features.py changed; FIELDS was extended so vocab sizing and X's second axis stay in sync, model and training loop untouched.
